statements.text: Among COSMIC variants in 19 TCGA head and neck genes, 86.9% were present at only one of the two tumour sub-sites sampled.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: COSMIC variants from 19 TCGA HNSCC genes demonstrated an 86.9% heterogeneity rate (present in one tumour sub-site only).
statements.note: The abstract reports exactly this heterogeneity rate for those variants.

statements.text: Plasma detection of tumour-specific variants was more sensitive in advanced-stage tumours than in early-stage disease.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Across all patients, cell-free DNA (ctDNA) identified 12.9% (range 7.5-19.8%) of tumour-specific variants, of which 55.6% were specific to a single tumour sub-site only.
statements.note: Detection rates are given per patient as a range, with no stratification by tumour stage.

statements.text: Circulating tumour DNA detected fewer than a quarter of the high-frequency tumour variants with variant allele frequency above 5%.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: CtDNA identified 79.0% (range: 55.6-90.9%) of high-frequency variants (tumour VAF>5%).
statements.note: The reported figure is 79.0%, far above a quarter.

statements.text: Across all patients ctDNA captured 12.9% of tumour-specific variants, but 79.0% of those present in tumour above 5% variant allele frequency.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Across all patients, cell-free DNA (ctDNA) identified 12.9% (range 7.5-19.8%) of tumour-specific variants, of which 55.6% were specific to a single tumour sub-site only. CtDNA identified 79.0% (range: 55.6-90.9%) of high-frequency variants (tumour VAF>5%).
statements.note: Both percentages are stated directly as results.

statements.text: Somatic CpG hypermutation showed no association with response to immune checkpoint inhibitors.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: We further observe an association between somatic CpG hypermutation and response to immune checkpoint inhibitors.
statements.note: An association with checkpoint inhibitor response is explicitly reported.

statements.text: Prevalence of somatic CpG hypermutation was highest in paediatric leukaemia at 3.5%, then paediatric high-grade glioma at 1.7% and colorectal cancer at 1%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Across cancer types, we observed the highest prevalence in paediatric leukaemia (3.5%), paediatric high-grade glioma (1.7%), and colorectal cancer (1%).
statements.note: These three prevalences are reported in this order.

statements.text: CpG deamination produces a higher tumour mutation burden than tobacco-associated mutational processes.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Somatic hypermutation in cancer has gained momentum with the increased use of tumour mutation burden as a biomarker for immune checkpoint inhibitors.
statements.note: Mutation burden appears only as background; no mutational process is compared with another.

statements.text: Germline variants and somatic mutations in the MutSa complex MSH2-MSH6 drove somatic CpG hypermutation, frequently converging on CpG sites and TP53 driver mutations.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We discovered germline variants and somatic mutations in the mismatch repair complex MutSα (MSH2-MSH6) as genetic drivers of somatic CpG hypermutation in cancer, which frequently converged on CpG sites and TP53 driver mutations.
statements.note: The abstract names MutSα alterations as the genetic drivers.

statements.text: Forty minutes of oxidation gave the greatest fall in total solid-phase abundance of resistance genes and mobile genetic elements, with markedly better dewaterability.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: At 40 min, sludge dewaterability was markedly improved, accompanied by the greatest reduction in the total abundance of ARGs and mobile genetic elements (MGEs) in solid phase.
statements.note: Both effects are reported for the 40-minute point.

statements.text: Prolonging the reaction from 40 to 60 minutes improved sludge dewaterability further.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: but accompanied by sludge dewaterability deterioration and a rebound in solid-associated ARGs and MGEs abundance
statements.note: Dewaterability deteriorated rather than improved at 60 minutes.

statements.text: The iron-activated peracetic acid process removed more resistance genes than conventional thermal hydrolysis conditioning of sludge.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Although advanced oxidation is promising for sludge conditioning, whether prolonged oxidation continuously benefits both dewatering and biological risk control remains unclear.
statements.note: Only the time course of this one process was tested; no alternative conditioning method was compared.

statements.text: Sixty minutes of reaction removed liquid-phase resistance genes and mobile elements most efficiently, while dewaterability worsened and solid-associated abundances rebounded.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Extending the reaction to 60 min achieved the highest removal efficiency for liquid phase ARGs and MGEs, while these ARGs-carrying pathogens remained inhibited; but accompanied by sludge dewaterability deterioration and a rebound in solid-associated ARGs and MGEs abundance.
statements.note: This split outcome at 60 minutes is stated as the result.

statements.text: Serial cell-free DNA measurement detected relapse earlier than imaging in these paediatric patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The use of specific CNAs as targets for liquid biopsy in pediatric patients with cancer can improve diagnosis and should be considered for monitoring of the disease response.
statements.note: Monitoring is only proposed; no timing comparison against imaging is reported.

statements.text: Of the tumour types sampled, neuroblastoma yielded the most cell-free DNA, and the amount tracked with tumour volume.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: neuroblastoma presented the greatest amount of cfDNA, in correlation with tumor volume
statements.note: The abstract reports both the ranking and the correlation with volume.

statements.text: Copy number levels agreed between tumour and circulating tumour DNA in 56% of cases at diagnosis; discordant alterations were mostly seen only in cell-free DNA.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: At diagnosis, CNAs levels were concordant between tumor and ctDNA in 56% of the cases, and for the remaining 44%, 91.4% of the CNAs were present only in cfDNA and 8.6% only in the tumor.
statements.note: Concordance was 56%, and 91.4% of discordant alterations were cfDNA-only.

statements.text: Within cell-free DNA, MYCN gain was seen in 23% of patients and 1q gain in 46%.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Within the cfDNA, we observed that 46% and 23% of the patients had MYCN and 1q gain, respectively.
statements.note: The figures are reversed: 46% MYCN and 23% 1q.

statements.text: After exclusions and quality control, 129 annotated scans from 91 patients remained, comprising 85 clear cell, 26 papillary and 18 chromophobe cases.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: After data exclusion and quality control, a final cohort of 129 annotated CT scans from 91 patients (24 female, 67 male; mean age 56 years) was retained, including 85 clear cell, 26 papillary and 18 chromophobe RCC cases.
statements.note: These are the stated final cohort numbers.

statements.text: Fewer than 200 CT scans were screened across the three TCGA renal cell carcinoma databases.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: we screened 1,915 CT scans from three TCGA-RCC databases
statements.note: The screen covered 1,915 scans, an order of magnitude more.

statements.text: Two trained students checked and corrected the annotations, and a board-certified radiologist reviewed the cases they found uncertain.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Two trained students performed quality checks, corrections, and additional annotation of tumors and cysts, with uncertain cases reviewed by a board-certified radiologist.
statements.note: The reader workflow is described exactly this way.

statements.text: Models trained on these annotations outperform radiologists at classifying renal cell carcinoma subtypes.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: RCC-AID provides a reusable open resource dataset for segmentation, detection, subtype classification, radiomics, and multimodal RCC research.
statements.note: The dataset is offered for subtype classification work, but no model performance or reader comparison is reported.

statements.text: Removing the Alu element from the F3 3'-UTR reduced tissue factor procoagulant activity at the cell surface.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Confocal microscopy of MDA-MB-231 human breast cancer cells using fluoroprobe constructs regulated by the F3 3'-UTR with or without the Alu insertion demonstrated that the presence of the Alu element promoted protein localisation to the Golgi, and reduced cell membrane localisation.
statements.note: Constructs without the Alu were tested for localisation only; no clotting or activity assay is reported.

statements.text: Constructs carrying the Alu element in the F3 3'-UTR showed more Golgi localisation and less cell membrane localisation than constructs without it.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: the presence of the Alu element promoted protein localisation to the Golgi, and reduced cell membrane localisation
statements.note: This is the reported microscopy result.

statements.text: Activating Protease-Activated Receptor-2 drove the fluorophore from the cell surface into the Golgi.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: stimulation of cells with a Protease-Activated Receptor-2 activating peptide led to rapid mobilisation of the fluorophore from the Golgi to the cell surface
statements.note: The movement reported runs the other way, Golgi to surface.

statements.text: The inverted Alu element inserted into the F3 3'-UTR roughly 30 to 40 million years ago.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Approximately 30-40 million years ago, an inverted Alu element inserted into the F3 3'-UTR
statements.note: The abstract dates the insertion to this window.

statements.text: A 19-gene risk score split patients into high- and low-risk groups with significantly different survival, and five of those genes were independent prognostic factors.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: A robust 19-gene signature was established to calculate risk scores, effectively categorizing patients into high- and low-risk groups with significantly divergent survival outcomes. From this signature, five genes were identified as independent prognostic factors via multivariable Cox analysis.
statements.note: Both the 19-gene signature and the five independent predictors are reported.

statements.text: Of the three core biomarkers, SMS is the one whose knockdown slows glioma cell proliferation in culture.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Ultimately, three prioritized core candidate biomarkers (AGMAT, PSMC5, and SMS) were extracted, among which SMS exhibited exceptionally high individual diagnostic efficacy.
statements.note: SMS stood out only in diagnostic performance; no cell-based functional experiment is reported.

statements.text: Predicted response to immunotherapy was better in the C1 subtype than in the C2 subtype.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: In contrast, the C2 subtype was characterized by robust immune cell infiltration, a more favorable prognosis, and a superior computationally predicted response to immunotherapy.
statements.note: The superior predicted response belongs to C2, not C1.

statements.text: The C1 subtype showed less immune infiltration, higher PD-L1 expression, elevated TIDE scores and poorer survival.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The C1 subtype exhibited a less immune-infiltrated phenotype but higher PD-L1 expression and elevated TIDE scores, indicating stronger immune evasion and poorer survival.
statements.note: This is the reported C1 phenotype.

statements.text: Histology showed an asymmetric melanocytic proliferation of epithelioid cells with brisk mitotic activity and dermal maturation.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Histopathologic examination revealed an asymmetric melanocytic proliferation composed predominantly of epithelioid cells with limited mitotic activity and evidence of dermal maturation.
statements.note: Mitotic activity was limited, not brisk.

statements.text: Immunohistochemistry was diffusely positive for Melan-A and SOX10, retained p16, and negative for PRAME.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Immunohistochemistry showed diffuse Melan-A and SOX10 positivity, retained p16 expression, a gradient HMB45 staining pattern, and negative PRAME expression.
statements.note: Each of these staining results is stated.

statements.text: Follow-up after excision showed no recurrence or metastasis in this patient.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Identification of an isolated RET fusion supports classification within the Spitz tumor spectrum and provides valuable information for risk stratification and clinical management in pediatric patients.
statements.note: The report closes on risk stratification and gives no clinical follow-up or outcome.

statements.text: Sequencing of the lesion in a 14-year-old girl found a RET::MXT1 fusion with no other pathogenic mutations and no copy number alterations.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: next-generation sequencing was performed and identified a RET::MXT1 gene fusion in the absence of additional pathogenic mutations or copy number alterations
statements.note: The fusion was the sole genomic finding in this case.

statements.text: The library held 46,389 unique transposable elements, 15,975 core and 30,414 variable, spanning about 1.04 Gb or 33.53% of the buffalo reference genome.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We identified 46,389 unique TE comprising 15,975 cores and 30,414 variable elements. These TE span approximately 1.04 Gb and its length account for 33.53% of the buffalo reference genome.
statements.note: All four figures are reported directly.

statements.text: Variable elements outnumbered core elements by roughly ten to one in the pan-TE library.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: We identified 46,389 unique TE comprising 15,975 cores and 30,414 variable elements.
statements.note: The real ratio is close to two to one.

statements.text: Core elements favoured genic regions, with DNA and LTR transposons often sitting inside gene introns.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Notably, these elements showed a preference for genic regions, with DNA and LTR transposons frequently located within gene introns.
statements.note: The genic preference and intronic location are both stated.

statements.text: Transposable element insertions explain the difference in milk yield between river and swamp buffalo.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Co-expression analysis identified several SINE-derived hub genes that played key roles in testicular and muscle tissue development.
statements.note: Expression links were drawn to testis and muscle development; no production trait is examined.

statements.text: Sensitivity was 90.5% with 93.8% specificity in the validation cohort, falling to 76.7% sensitivity with 92.9% specificity in the external cohort.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In the validation cohort, the model demonstrated a sensitivity of 90.5% and specificity of 93.8%, while in the external cohort, it exhibited a sensitivity of 76.7% and specificity of 92.9%.
statements.note: These are the stated cohort-specific performance figures.

statements.text: The model was developed in a cohort of fewer than 60 renal cell carcinoma patients.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: A total of 280 participants, including 142 RCC patients and 138 noncancer controls, were enrolled for model development.
statements.note: Development used 142 patients alongside 138 controls.

statements.text: Performance held across TNM stages, histological subtypes and Fuhrman grades, with high sensitivity even in early-stage renal cell carcinoma.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Robust performance was observed across different TNM (tumor-node-metastasis) stages, histological subtypes, and Fuhrman grades, with high sensitivity even for early-stage RCC.
statements.note: Robustness across these strata is reported explicitly.

statements.text: Using the assay for annual screening lowered renal cell carcinoma mortality.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The cfDNA fragmentomics-based liquid biopsy provides a promising, noninvasive, cost-effective, and accurate approach for RCC detection and management, substantiating its potential as a complementary tool to conventional diagnostic techniques.
statements.note: Only diagnostic accuracy was measured; no screening programme or mortality outcome was studied.

statements.text: The island encodes no conjugation apparatus of its own but carries an origin of transfer sharing about 85% nucleotide identity with the co-resident ICE.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: GISsuJHJ17_rpsI lacks a self-encoded conjugation apparatus but harbours an origin of transfer (oriT) sharing ∼85% nucleotide identity with the co-resident integrative and conjugative element (ICE)
statements.note: Both the missing apparatus and the ~85% identity are stated.

statements.text: The island also transferred into Staphylococcus aureus recipients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: These findings show that GISsuJHJ17_rpsI can transfer from S. suis to E. faecalis and integrate at an rpsI-associated site.
statements.note: Transfer was shown into E. faecalis and the S. suis recipient model only; no other recipient species was tested.

statements.text: Deleting either the ICE relaxase or the island's oriT abolished verified transconjugants, and complementation or oriT repair restored detectable transfer.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Deletion of either determinant yielded no verified transconjugants under the assay conditions, whereas relaxase complementation and chromosomal oriT repair restored detectable transfer.
statements.note: This loss and restoration of transfer is the reported result.

statements.text: Acquiring the genomic island imposed a clear growth defect and a competitive disadvantage on transconjugants.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Fitness assays revealed no measurable growth defect or competitive disadvantage associated with acquisition of GISsuJHJ17_rpsI, indicating a minimal short-term fitness cost.
statements.note: Neither a growth defect nor a competitive disadvantage was measurable.

statements.text: Knocking down SETDB1 restored expression of silenced tumour suppressor genes in breast cancer cells.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: However, some potential biomarkers still remain unexplored, like SETDB1, a histone methyltransferase involved in epigenetic silencing of tumor suppressor genes.
statements.note: SETDB1's silencing role is background; this study analysed mutation and survival data and ran no knockdown.

statements.text: Mutation in SETDB1, USP37, NDUFS1, TRPM4 and MYO18A was associated with poor prognosis, NDUFS1 being the weakest of the five at p = 0.025.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: SETDB1 (p < 0.0001), USP37 (p < 0.0001), NDUFS1 (p = 0.025), TRPM4 (p < 0.0001), and MYO18A (p < 0.0001) were associated with poor prognosis.
statements.note: All five genes and their p values are listed as prognostic.

statements.text: Survival data were available for 845 cases and mutation data for all but two of them.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: A total of 845 cases of breast carcinoma with complete survival data were retrieved, of which mutation data for 800 cases were available.
statements.note: Mutation data covered 800 of the 845 cases, not all but two.

statements.text: ARMCX5 and SLCO6A1 were enriched in high-grade breast tumours.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: ARMCX5 (p < 0.0001) and SLCO6A1 (p < 0.0001) were enriched in high-grade tumors.
statements.note: Both genes are reported as enriched in high-grade tumours.

statements.text: Two proteins encoded by the element, RamT and RamA, acted in recipient cells to inhibit both the SOS response and homologous recombination after transfer.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: RamT and RamA that modulate the SOS response in donors also function in recipient cells to inhibit both the SOS response and homologous recombination following transfer of the element
statements.note: The abstract reports this recipient-side activity for both proteins.

statements.text: RamA bound PcrA and blocked the translocase's removal of RecA from DNA.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: We found that RamA interacted with PcrA, the host DNA translocase that functions to remove RecA from DNA, likely functioning to modulate the SOS response and recombination by stimulating PcrA activity
statements.note: RamA is proposed to stimulate PcrA, not block it.

statements.text: Cells that received the element were more sensitive to killing by ultraviolet irradiation.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: ICE Bs1 of Bacillus subtilis modulates the host DNA damage response by reducing RecA filament formation.
statements.note: Effects are described at the level of RecA filaments and SOS signalling; no survival after DNA damage is reported.

statements.text: Expressing RamT and RamA reduced binding of the host single-strand binding protein SsbA to single-stranded DNA.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Expression of RamT and RamA caused a decrease in binding of the host single strand binding protein SsbA to ssDNA.
statements.note: This decrease in SsbA binding is a stated result.

statements.text: Drinking at least 15 g of alcohol daily carried a hazard ratio of 2.43 for c-dMMRb/SBS26-high colorectal cancer relative to nondrinkers.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Compared with nondrinkers, drinkers who imbibed 15 g/d or more of alcohol had a high risk of c-dMMRb/SBS26-high CRC (multivariable-adjusted hazard ratio = 2.43, 95% confidence interval = 1.55 to 3.82)
statements.note: The hazard ratio of 2.43 is reported for this subtype.

statements.text: Alcohol intake of 15 g/d or more was also significantly associated with c-dMMRb/SBS26-low colorectal cancer.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: but not c-dMMRb/SBS26-low CRC (multivariable-adjusted hazard ratio = 0.86, 95% confidence interval = 0.57 to 1.28)
statements.note: For the signature-low subtype the confidence interval crosses one, so no association was found.

statements.text: No significant difference in the alcohol association appeared across levels of the c-dMMRa/SBS15 signature.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: No significant differential associations were observed for c-dMMRa/SBS15 (Ptrend = .41 for heterogeneity).
statements.note: Heterogeneity by SBS15 contribution was not significant.

statements.text: Beer drinkers showed a stronger association with signature-high colorectal cancer than wine drinkers.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Dietary data were collected every 4 years through validated food frequency questionnaires.
statements.note: Intake was analysed in grams per day, with no breakdown by beverage type.

statements.text: Six variant callers were benchmarked, two of them UMI-aware, UMI-VarCal and UMIErrorCorrect, against the standard callers Mutect2, bcftools, LoFreq and FreeBayes.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In this study, we benchmarked six variant calling tools, including two UMI-aware callers for their ability to call ctDNA variants. The standard variant callers tested included Mutect2, bcftools, LoFreq and FreeBayes. The UMI-aware variant callers benchmarked were UMI-VarCal and UMIErrorCorrect.
statements.note: The abstract lists exactly these six tools in these two groups.

statements.text: In data encoded with synthetic UMIs, UMI-VarCal produced more putative false positive variants than every other caller tested.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: In data encoded with synthetic UMIs, UMI-VarCal detected fewer putative false positive variants than all other callers in synthetic datasets.
statements.note: UMI-VarCal produced the fewest putative false positives, not the most.

statements.text: Mutect2 was highly sensitive but, in data lacking synthetic UMIs, returned more privately called variants than any other caller, pointing to false positives.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Mutect2 showed high sensitivity, while returning more privately called variants than any other caller in data without synthetic UMIs - an indicator of false positive variant discovery.
statements.note: This combination of high sensitivity and excess private calls is reported for Mutect2.

statements.text: UMI-aware callers took substantially longer to run than the standard callers.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Variant callers displayed different preferences for sensitivity and specificity.
statements.note: The comparison covered sensitivity and specificity only; runtime and compute cost are never mentioned.

statements.text: Ultra-deep sequencing raised KRAS detection by 46%, finding mutations in the same 11 patients plus 7 more called negative by the standard assay.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Ultra-deep sequencing demonstrated a 46% increase in detection, identifying mutant KRAS in these same 11 patients and an additional 7 patients deemed mutation-negative by standard assay.
statements.note: The 46% gain and the extra 7 patients are both reported.

statements.text: Serial circulating tumour DNA testing during chemotherapy identified progression before imaging in these patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: This study aimed to investigate the prognostic potential of KRAS G12, G13, and Q61 mutations present in circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) prior to treatment initiation in localized PDAC using both standard depth (20,000x) and ultra-deep (≥100,000) sequencing.
statements.note: Only pre-treatment baseline plasma was analysed; no on-treatment sampling or imaging comparison is reported.

statements.text: Plasma was collected from 45 patients with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma before treatment.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Plasma samples were collected from 45 patients with non-metastatic PDAC prior to treatment start.
statements.note: The 45 patients had non-metastatic disease.

statements.text: Baseline KRAS detection by ultra-deep sequencing predicted worse overall survival with hazard ratio 3.13, while standard-depth detection did not reach significance.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Presence of any KRAS mutation at baseline by standard sequencing was not significantly associated with overall survival (OS) (HR 2.57, 95% CI 0.94-7.04). However, detection of any KRAS mutation by ultra-deep sequencing in baseline ctDNA was significantly predictive of worse OS (HR 3.13, 95% CI 1.18-8.29).
statements.note: Only the ultra-deep assay reached significance, at HR 3.13.

statements.text: Recurrent urinary tract infections involved multiple pandemic UPEC lineages, including ST131, ST69, ST10 and the emerging ST1193.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Recurrent urinary tract infections (UTIs) were associated with multiple pandemic UPEC lineages, including ST131, ST69, ST10 and the emerging ST1193.
statements.note: These four lineages are named as the ones involved.

statements.text: Among the predicted plasmids, IncF replicons were the least common type identified.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: MOB-suite plasmid prediction analysis showed that IncF replicons were the most common and frequently associated with ESBL genes.
statements.note: IncF replicons were the most common, not the least.

statements.text: Patients who received autovaccine therapy had fewer recurrences than those treated with antibiotics.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Whole-genome sequencing was performed on 199 UPEC isolates recovered from patients with recurrent or difficult-to-treat UTIs for whom autovaccine therapy was recommended.
statements.note: Autovaccine therapy explains how the isolates were collected; no treatment outcomes are reported.

statements.text: Nearly 80% of the isolates carried acquired antimicrobial resistance genes, among them the ESBL genes blaCTX-M-15 and blaCTX-M-27.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Genomic analyses identified acquired antimicrobial resistance genes in nearly 80% of isolates, including extended-spectrum β -lactamase (ESBL) genes such as bla CTX-M-15 and bla CTX-M-27
statements.note: The abstract gives nearly 80% and names these two ESBL genes.

statements.text: Recurrently rearranged regions were shared across the five cancer types rather than being specific to one.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Recurrently mutated regions tend to be cancer-type specific and overlap with cancer genes, suggesting that selection contributes to shaping the SV landscape.
statements.note: Those regions tended to be cancer-type specific.

statements.text: Complex structural variants were found in 56 tumours, 47% of the cohort, with different classes appearing across several cancer types.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Complex SVs were identified in 56 tumors (47%) and different classes occurred across multiple cancer types.
statements.note: The count and percentage are reported directly.

statements.text: Complex structural variants were more frequent in tumours from older children than in those from infants.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: In a cohort of 120 primary tumors, we systematically characterized patterns of extrachromosomal DNA, chromoplexy and chromothripsis across five pediatric solid cancer types: neuroblastoma, Ewing sarcoma, Wilms tumor, hepatoblastoma and rhabdomyosarcoma.
statements.note: Frequencies are broken down by cancer type; patient age is never mentioned.

statements.text: Potentially pathogenic complex variants were found in 42 tumours, half of them known drivers such as ecDNA-driven MYCN amplification and chromoplexy-derived EWSR1::FLI1 fusions.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In total, we identified potentially pathogenic complex SVs in 42 tumors that affect cancer driver genes or result in unfavorable chromosomal alterations. Half of which were known drivers, e.g. MYCN amplifications due to ecDNA and EWSR1::FLI1 fusions due to chromoplexy.
statements.note: Both the count of 42 and the two example drivers are stated.

statements.text: LINE-1 methylation in plasma cell-free DNA and in tissue was significantly lower in grade 4 gliomas than in controls.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: LINE-1 methylation content in plasma cfDNA and tissue samples was decreased significantly in grade 4 gliomas compared to controls
statements.note: Both sample types showed the significant decrease in grade 4 cases.

statements.text: Cell-free LINE-1 methylation was inversely correlated with LINE-1 methylation measured in matched tissue.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: cfLINE-1 methylation was positively correlated with tissue LINE-1 methylation levels
statements.note: The reported correlation is positive.

statements.text: DNMT1, H4K20me3 and H3K9me3 expression was significantly reduced in grade 4 cases compared with grade 2 cases.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Similarly, DNMT1, H4K20me3 and H3K9me3 expression was significantly reduced in grade 4 cases compared to grade 2
statements.note: This grade 4 versus grade 2 reduction is reported for all three markers.

statements.text: Plasma LINE-1 methylation rose again after surgical resection of the glioma.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: LINE-1 methylation was measured in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) of glioma patients' plasma prior to surgery or any adjuvant therapy and age-matched controls as well as in glioma tissues along with DNMT1, H4K20me3 and H3K9me3 expression.
statements.note: Plasma was sampled only before surgery or adjuvant therapy, so no post-treatment change was measured.

statements.text: At least 26% of the 706 characterised IS3 elements are estimated to already carry promoters.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We also estimate that at least 26% of the 706 characterized IS3s already encode promoters.
statements.note: Both the 26% estimate and the 706 elements are stated.

statements.text: Promoters arising in IS3 ends raised expression of neighbouring host genes enough to improve host fitness.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Our observations can help to explain why mobile DNA may persist in prokaryotic genomes.
statements.note: Persistence is offered as an interpretation; promoter strength was measured in a reporter assay, with no host gene expression or fitness measurement.

statements.text: All ten sequences taken from the ends of five IS3 elements gained de novo promoter activity from single point mutations, among 18,537 mutations tested.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We started with 10 sequences from the ends of 5 IS3 sequences, created 18,537 random mutations in them, and measured their promoter activity using a massively parallel reporter assay. All 10 sequences could evolve de-novo promoter activity from single point mutations.
statements.note: Every one of the ten sequences evolved promoter activity from single point mutations.

statements.text: The ends of IS3 elements contain about half as many proto-promoter sequences as the E. coli genome does.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The ends of IS3s harbor ~1.5 times as many such proto-promoter sequences than the E. coli genome.
statements.note: IS3 ends carry about 1.5 times as many, not half as many.

statements.text: Jujube centromeres are built mainly of Gypsy-type long terminal repeat retrotransposons rather than the tandem repeat-rich arrays seen in many plants.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Unlike the TR-rich centromeres found in many plant species, jujube centromeres are predominantly composed of Gypsy -type long-terminal repeat retrotransposons (LTR-RTs).
statements.note: This composition is the central reported finding.

statements.text: The CRJ family is still transpositionally active in the jujube genome today.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Notably, early insertions of CRJ-derived LTR segments contributed to the formation of TR-like structures, suggesting a mechanistic link between transposable elements and the evolution of centromeric tandem repeats.
statements.note: Only ancient CRJ insertions and their structural legacy are described; current activity is not assessed.

statements.text: Across plant species, centromeric retrotransposons were spread evenly over many unrelated subfamilies, showing no subfamily specificity.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Comparative analysis across plant species revealed that centromeric retrotransposons primarily fall into three subfamilies- CRM , Tekay , and Athila -highlighting strong subfamily specificity.
statements.note: They fall into three subfamilies with strong specificity.

statements.text: The CENH3-defined centromeres ranged from 0.75 to 1.40 Mb and were largely conserved between haplotypes apart from a local inversion on chromosome 10.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: These centromeres, ranging from 0.75 to 1.40 Mb, are largely conserved between haplotypes, except for a localized inversion on chromosome 10.
statements.note: The size range and the single chromosome 10 exception are both reported.

statements.text: Signature scores were measured in 84 cell-free DNA samples from 46 high-risk patients, 21 of whom contributed serial samples.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We then quantified signature scores, and our prior neuroblastoma signature, in cfDNA from 84 samples from 46 high-risk patients including 21 patients with serial samples.
statements.note: These are the stated sample and patient counts.

statements.text: In serially collected samples the adrenergic and mesenchymal scores moved in opposite directions.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: While ADRN and MES signature scores tracked together in serially collected samples, we identified instances of patients with increases in either MES or ADRN score at relapse.
statements.note: The two scores tracked together in serial samples.

statements.text: Patients with greater metastatic burden had higher GSVA scores for both the adrenergic and the mesenchymal gene signatures.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Samples from patients with higher metastatic burden had increased GSVA scores for both ADRN and MES gene signatures (p < 0.001).
statements.note: Both signatures rose with metastatic burden.

statements.text: The mesenchymal signature score at diagnosis predicted overall survival in these high-risk patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: While it is feasible to identify ADRN and MES signatures using 5-hmC profiles of cfDNA from neuroblastoma patients and correlate these signatures to metastatic burden, additional data are needed to determine the optimal strategies for clinical implementation.
statements.note: Scores were related to metastatic burden only; no survival analysis is reported.

statements.text: Combination treatment extended survival of animals in the PARPi-resistant mouse model.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Here, we demonstrate that inhibition of epigenetic modifiers euchromatic histone lysine methyltransferases 1/2 (EHMT1/2) reduces the growth of multiple PARPi-resistant ovarian cancer cell lines and tumor growth in a PARPi-resistant mouse model of ovarian cancer.
statements.note: Tumour growth was the in vivo readout; animal survival is not reported.

statements.text: Epigenomic profiling placed EHMT2 on transposable elements, and EHMT inhibition derepressed those elements genome-wide, both epigenetically and transcriptionally.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we found that EHMT2 is bound to transposable elements, and that EHMT inhibition leads to genome-wide epigenetic and transcriptional derepression of transposable elements
statements.note: Binding and derepression are both reported results.

statements.text: Combined EHMT and PARP inhibition reduced immunostimulatory double-stranded RNA formation in vitro.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: We found that combinatory EHMT and PARP inhibition increases immunostimulatory double-stranded RNA formation and elicits several immune signaling pathways in vitro.
statements.note: Double-stranded RNA formation increased with the combination.

statements.text: In a PARPi-resistant syngeneic mouse model, combined EHMT and PARP inhibition slowed tumour progression and raised the number of Granzyme B-positive cells.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In a PARPi-resistant syngeneic murine model, EHMT and PARP inhibition combination inhibited tumor progression and increased Granzyme B+ cells in the tumor.
statements.note: Both effects are reported for the syngeneic model.

statements.text: Efflux was the dominant resistance mechanism in the resistome, ahead of antibiotic inactivation.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Resistance mechanisms were predominantly driven by antibiotic inactivation, followed by efflux and target protection.
statements.note: Inactivation came first, with efflux second.

statements.text: Metagenomic analysis identified 489 unique resistance genes covering 29 antibiotic classes in the wastewater samples.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: A total of 489 unique ARGs conferring resistance to 29 antibiotic classes were identified through metagenomic analysis.
statements.note: Both counts are reported directly.

statements.text: Resistance gene abundance was higher in hospital wastewater than in community wastewater.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: were detected across both hospital and community wastewater samples
statements.note: Presence in both settings is reported; the abstract makes no abundance comparison between them.

statements.text: Of 103 dereplicated metagenome-assembled genomes, 80 carried resistance genes and 26 held putative mobile resistance regions within 10 kb.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Genome-resolved analysis reconstructed 103 dereplicated MAGs, of which 80 carried ARGs and 26 contained putative mobile resistance regions defined by ARG–MGE co-localizations within 10 kb.
statements.note: All three counts and the 10 kb definition are stated.

statements.text: C>T substitutions predominated, and the signatures SBS22 and SBS43 were enriched in Luminal A tumours.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Mutational signature analysis revealed a predominance of C>T substitutions and subtype-specific patterns, with SBS22 and SBS43 enriched in Luminal A tumors.
statements.note: Both the substitution bias and the subtype enrichment are reported.

statements.text: The mutational landscape of these tumours differed significantly from that of European breast cancers in TCGA.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Yet, genomic data from Middle Eastern and North African (MENA) populations are limited, restricting insights into disease drivers and therapeutic opportunities in this demographic.
statements.note: The data gap motivates the study, but no comparison against another population's cohort is reported.

statements.text: Driver prediction flagged 2451 mutations, of which 648 were known driver variants and 1803 were novel predictions.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: driver prediction tools (BoostDM and OncodriveMUT) identified 2451 predicted driver mutations, including 648 known driver variants in genes such as TP53, PIK3CA, GATA3, PTEN, SF3B1, and KMT2C. In addition, 1803 novel predicted drivers were detected
statements.note: These three counts are reported directly.

statements.text: Annotation with OncoKB found no actionable or likely oncogenic variants in the cohort.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Therapeutic annotation using OncoKB identified 223 actionable or likely oncogenic variants, highlighting potential targets for precision oncology.
statements.note: OncoKB annotation identified 223 such variants.

statements.text: In the TCGA cohort, RNA analysis revealed previously unreported mutations in BAP1 in three tumours and EIF1AX in five, missed by the original DNA sequencing.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Notably, in the TCGA cohort we detected previously unreported mutations in BAP1 (n = 3) and EIF1AX (n = 5), that were missed by the original DNA sequencing.
statements.note: Both counts and the fact they were missed by DNA sequencing are stated.

statements.text: Unsupervised expression profiling reliably identified every class of genetic alteration tested.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Whereas unsupervised gene expression profiling strongly indicated the presence of chromosome 3 alterations, it was not reliable in identifying other alterations.
statements.note: It worked for chromosome 3 but was unreliable for other alterations.

statements.text: Copy number alterations of chromosome 3 and 8q were inferred from expressed allelic imbalance at heterozygous common single nucleotide polymorphisms.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: the presence of both chromosome 3 and 8q copy number alterations could be successfully inferred from expressed allelic imbalances of heterozygous common single nucleotide polymorphisms
statements.note: This inference route is reported as successful for both regions.

statements.text: RNA sequencing costs less per sample than the DNA sequencing it could replace.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: In conclusion, a transcriptional analysis presents insights into the expressed tumour genotype and its phenotypic consequences and may augment or even substitute DNA-based approaches, with potential applicability in research and clinical practice.
statements.note: Substitution is argued on detection grounds; no cost comparison is reported.

statements.text: Every lavage sample contained multiple TP53 mutant clones, which were used to compute the mutation burden frequency.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: All lavages contained multiple TP53 mutant clones, which were used to quantify TP53 mutation burden frequency (MBF).
statements.note: All lavages carried multiple mutant clones.

statements.text: Uterine lavage mutation burden was also raised in patients with endometrial cancer.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Here we investigate if TP53 mutation burden measured in uterine lavage, a minimally invasive gynecological liquid biopsy, can discriminate between patients with and without HGSC.
statements.note: The comparison was high grade serous cancer versus none; no other malignancy is examined.

statements.text: Removing the tumour's clonal TP53 mutations from the calculation abolished the association with ovarian cancer.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Excluding tumor TP53 clonal mutations from the lavage MBF calculation maintains this association, suggesting that it is the overall TP53 somatic mutation burden (rather than the discovery of the specific tumor driver mutation) that identifies HGSC.
statements.note: The association was maintained after excluding those clonal mutations.

statements.text: In average-risk patients, higher TP53 mutation burden frequency identified high grade serous ovarian cancer with 77% sensitivity, 89% specificity and an AUC of 0.88.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Average risk patients with HGSC had significantly higher TP53 MBF independently of age and other risk factors (77% sensitivity, 89% specificity, AUC = 0.88).
statements.note: These three performance figures are reported for average-risk patients.

statements.text: A screen across 43 drosophilid species yielded five conserved genes derived from Tc1/mariner transposases.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We performed a systematic genomic screen across 43 drosophilid species using stringent criteria for molecular domestication. This analysis identified five high-confidence, evolutionarily conserved genes derived from Tc1/mariner transposases.
statements.note: Both the species count and the five genes are stated.

statements.text: Co-expression analysis linked toy to cell cycle and chromosome functions and CG4570 to neuronal development.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: CG14478 is linked to RNA/chromatin-related processes, CG4570 to cell cycle/chromosome functions, cag to ciliary and nuclear functions, and toy to neuronal development.
statements.note: The assignments are swapped: CG4570 to cell cycle, toy to neuronal development.

statements.text: Only CG14478 represented the catalytic-domain route, and structural modelling showed its protein keeps a canonical DDE endonuclease fold.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In contrast, the catalytic domain pathway is represented solely by CG14478. Structural modeling reveals that CG14478 protein preserves a canonical DDE endonuclease fold.
statements.note: CG14478 is the sole catalytic-domain case and retains the DDE fold.

statements.text: Flies with CG14478 deleted show defects in chromosome segregation.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: This study establishes a stringent framework for identifying domesticated TEs, demonstrating that Tc1/mariner elements are co-opted via two distinct pathways: retention of either catalytic or DNA-binding modules.
statements.note: Roles were inferred from sequence, structure and co-expression; no mutant phenotype is reported.

statements.text: Cancer-type-specific models reached F1 scores up to 90% for skin cutaneous melanoma and 89% for skin adenocarcinoma, against 79.2% for the pan-cancer baseline.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Cancer-type-specific models significantly outperformed a baseline pan-cancer model, achieving a maximum leave-one-group-out cross-validation (LOGO-CV) F1 score of up to 90% for CanDrivRSKCM (Skin Cutaneous Melanoma) and 89% for CanDrivR-SKCA (Skin Adenocarcinoma) , compared to 79.2% for the baseline model.
statements.note: All three F1 values are reported.

statements.text: Recurrent variants predicted by the models were enriched in genes targeted by approved drugs.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Moreover, studies have demonstrated the significance of rare mutations that arise as resistance mechanisms in response to drug treatment.
statements.note: Drug-resistance mutations are cited as background; predictions are never linked to drug targets.

statements.text: The models were built to separate variants seen in cancer from those seen in healthy populations.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Here, we introduce CanDrivR-CS , a set of cancer-specific gradient boosting models designed to distinguish between rare and recurrent cancer variants.
statements.note: The models separate rare from recurrent cancer variants, a contrast within cancer genomes.

statements.text: DNA shape properties ranked consistently among the top discriminating features, with recurrent missense variants often falling in DNA bends and rolls.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Notably, DNA shape properties consistently ranked among the top features for distinguishing recurrent and rare variants across all cancers. Specifically, recurrent missense variants frequently occurred in DNA bends and rolls
statements.note: Feature importance and the bend and roll preference are both reported.

statements.text: With cross-validated linear discriminant analysis, accuracy rose from 71.1% under non-polarized excitation to 93.9% with fused dual-polarization spectra, beating polynomial-fitting SERS throughout.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Using 5-fold cross-validated linear discriminant analysis, SE-SERDS consistently outperformed PF-SERS across all excitation modes, with prediction accuracies rising from 71.1 vs 66.7% (NP) to a maximum of 93.9 vs 87.8% (LHCP + RHCP).
statements.note: Those accuracies and the consistent advantage over PF-SERS are reported.

statements.text: Spectra were collected from 90 patients in total, half of whom later had a recurrence.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Spectra were acquired from 90 recurrent and 90 non-recurrent NPC patients under non-polarized (NP), left-handed circularly polarized (LHCP), and right-handed circularly polarized (RHCP) excitations, alongside a fused LHCP + RHCP dataset.
statements.note: There were 90 recurrent plus 90 non-recurrent patients, so 180 in all.

statements.text: The two prognostic bands at 1074 and 1147 cm-1 arise from methylated cytosine in the cell-free DNA.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: enabling the extraction of subtle prognostic features at 1074 and 1147 cm-1 with a higher signal-to-background contrast
statements.note: The bands are reported as discriminative features with no molecular assignment given.

statements.text: Replacing linear discriminant analysis with a support vector machine raised accuracy further, to 95.6%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Integration with a support vector machine (SVM) further enhanced the accuracy to 95.6%.
statements.note: The support vector machine reached 95.6%.

statements.text: Small RNAs pulled down with PmAgo4 from testis were mostly 26 to 27 nucleotides long, indicating PmAgo4 associates predominantly with piRNAs.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: RNA-seq revealed a majority of 26-27 nt long small RNAs in the PmAgo4-IP fraction suggesting that PmAgo4 is predominantly associated with piRNAs.
statements.note: The size class and the piRNA conclusion are both reported.

statements.text: Most transposon-mapping piRNAs came from the sense strand of the gypsy and mariner-like elements.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Mapping of these piRNAs on nucleotide sequences of two gypsy and a mariner-like transposons of P. monodon suggested that most piRNAs were originated from the antisense strand of transposons.
statements.note: Most piRNAs came from the antisense strand.

statements.text: Knocking down PmAgo4 with a specific double-stranded RNA raised expression of the three transposons and lowered transposon-related piRNA levels.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Suppression of PmAgo4 expression by a specific dsRNA elevated the expression levels of the three transposons while decreasing the levels of transposon-related piRNAs.
statements.note: Both directions of change are reported after knockdown.

statements.text: PmAgo4 also silences transposons in shrimp somatic tissues such as the hepatopancreas.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: This study explored a molecular mechanism by which PmAgo4 regulates transposon expression in the shrimp germline.
statements.note: All experiments used testis and were framed around the germline; somatic tissues are not examined.

statements.text: Across glucose-, phosphate- and sulfate-limited conditions, 95 replicate yeast populations were evolved in miniature chemostats and then whole-genome sequenced.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we generated a highly parallel set of yeast evolution experiments in glucose-, phosphate-, and sulfate-limited media conditions with a total of 95 replicates across the conditions. Whole genome sequencing of the resulting populations allowed us to analyze recurrent targets of mutation during these evolution experiments.
statements.note: The replicate count and the sequencing of the evolved populations are both stated.

statements.text: Populations carrying new Ty insertions reached higher fitness than those carrying only point mutations.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Comparing the frequency of genes impacted by either SNPs and indels or Ty1/Ty2 elements, we find that a gene's location relative to predictors of Ty element mobilization likely impacted whether a gene was affected by either mutational modality.
statements.note: The comparison concerned which genes each modality hit, not the fitness of the populations.

statements.text: Mutational targets differed by limitation: the SAGA complex under sulfate limitation, sirtuins under phosphate limitation, and the phosphorelay system under glucose limitation.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we found consistent targeting of complexes and pathways, such as the SAGA complex in sulfate limitation, the sirtuin family in phosphate limitation, and the phosphorelay signal transduction system in glucose limitation.
statements.note: Each pathway is tied to its limitation exactly this way.

statements.text: New mobilizations of Ty1 and Ty2 elements landed in genes that were never affected by SNPs or indels in other populations.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: We also recurrently observed new mobilizations of Ty1 and Ty2 transposable elements, often interrupting genes that were also separately mutated by SNPs/InDels in other populations.
statements.note: Those insertions often hit genes that other populations mutated by SNPs or indels.

statements.text: The analysis covered 252 treatment-naive primary testicular germ cell tumours with deep whole-genome sequencing plus matched transcriptomic and epigenomic data.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Here we present a comprehensive genomic analysis of 252 treatment-naive primary TGCTs, integrating deep whole-genome sequencing with matched transcriptomic and epigenomic data.
statements.note: The cohort size and the three data types are stated.

statements.text: Seminomas showed greater structural complexity and subclonal diversity than non-seminomas.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: while non-seminomas show greater structural complexity, subclonal diversity, relatively earlier-onset WGD, extended tumor latency, and telomere elongation
statements.note: Greater structural complexity and subclonal diversity belong to non-seminomas.

statements.text: SBS87 burden predicted response to platinum chemotherapy in these tumours.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: SBS87 is linked to extended tumor latency and telomere elongation, implicating possible environmental or endogenous processes that mimic thiopurine-induced DNA damage in TGCT pathogenesis.
statements.note: SBS87 is related to latency and telomere length; no treatment-response analysis is reported.

statements.text: Whole genome doubling was ubiquitous in these tumours, happened developmentally early, and was associated with age at onset.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: whole genome doubling (WGD) in TGCTs is further characterized here as ubiquitous, developmentally early, and associated with age at onset
statements.note: All three characterisations of whole genome doubling are stated.

statements.text: Five recurrent cancer driver mutations were found, spanning MUC16, MUC4, ALK and CTNND1, the last being novel and carrying the missense change R439C.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we identified five recurrent cancer driver mutations spanning MUC16 , MUC4 , ALK , and CTNND1 , with the latter being novel and containing a missense mutation, R439C.
statements.note: The five drivers, the four genes and the R439C change are all stated.

statements.text: Patients whose tumours carried ALK F1174L were treated with an ALK inhibitor.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: We also identified 11 putative actionable mutations including NF1 Q1798*, Q2616*, and S636X, ALK F1174L and R1275Q, SETD2 P10L and Q1829E, BRCA1 R612S, NOTCH1 D1670V, ATR S1372L, and FGFR1 N577K.
statements.note: Actionability is a computational prediction; no treatment given to patients is reported.

statements.text: Exome sequencing covered more than 300 frozen neuroblastoma tumour samples from the Biobank.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: we conducted the whole-exome sequencing of 48 freshly frozen tumor samples obtained from the Biobank
statements.note: Sequencing covered 48 samples.

statements.text: The most frequently mutated genes were MUC4, MUC16 and FLG, and the commonest mutational signature was single base substitution 5.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The most common mutational signature was single base substitution 5. MUC4 , MUC16 , and FLG were identified as the most frequently mutated genes.
statements.note: Both the gene ranking and the dominant signature are reported.

statements.text: Polyposis, gastric cancer and early-onset colorectal cancer occurred in biallelic MCM8 carriers as well as in biallelic MCM9 carriers.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: we documented polyposis, gastric cancer, and early-onset colorectal cancer in 6, 1, and 6 biallelic MCM9 variant carriers, respectively, while these phenotypes were not observed in biallelic MCM8 variant carriers
statements.note: These phenotypes were seen only in MCM9 carriers.

statements.text: Tumours from carriers with germline sequencing data mostly showed the clock-like signatures SBS1 and SBS5, with no DNA repair deficiency signatures.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Tumors from MCM8 / MCM9 variant carriers with available germline sequencing data predominantly displayed clock-like mutational processes (single base substitution signatures 1 and 5), with no evidence of signatures associated with DNA repair deficiencies.
statements.note: Clock-like signatures dominated and repair-deficiency signatures were absent.

statements.text: Biallelic MCM9 variants were significantly enriched among rectal polyp cases, odds ratio 8.40, and gastric cancer cases, odds ratio 27.03.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: rectal polyps (OR 8.40, 95% CI 1.28–55.35; P = 0.03), and gastric cancer (OR 27.03, 95% CI 2.93– 248.5; P = 0.004)
statements.note: Both odds ratios are reported as significant enrichments.

statements.text: Heterozygous carriers of a single MCM9 loss-of-function variant also have raised colorectal cancer risk.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: this study aimed to delineate the molecular and clinical characteristics of individuals with biallelic germline MCM8 / MCM9 variants
statements.note: Every analysis concerns biallelic carriers; monoallelic carriers are not evaluated.
